name: live_coalesce_with_empty_string_default_is_null_on_oracle
description: COALESCE over a nullable column with an EMPTY string default is non-nullable on every engine except Oracle, which stores '' as NULL; the analyzer must be dialect-aware here or it renders a non-optional column that Oracle then returns NULL for
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name ListUserEmailsWithEmptyDefault
-- @returns :many
SELECT id, COALESCE(email, '') AS email_or_empty FROM users ORDER BY id

columns.name: email_or_empty
columns.note: '' is a value distinct from NULL under this fixture's default (PostgreSQL) dialect, so the COALESCE fallback really does guarantee non-NULL there

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc marks the COALESCE result nullable on every engine because its first argument is nullable, so it never has to decide what '' means
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe infers non-nullable from the literal fallback, which is correct everywhere except Oracle -- and this fixture is the one that forces that exception to be real inference rather than a footnote, by making Oracle return the NULL

default: INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (1, 'Ada Lovelace', 'ada@example.com')
INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (2, 'Grace Hopper', NULL)

oracle.reason: Oracle stores the empty string as NULL, so COALESCE(email, '') falls back to a value that is itself NULL. This is a real semantic difference in the engine, not a defect in the fixture -- and it is exactly why the analyzer's nullability for this expression has to depend on the dialect.
